Issued at 220 AM CDT Tue Sep 8 2026

The upper ridge that has been responsible for our near record 
warm first week of September is poised to be suppressed 
southward a bit mid week as a pair of shortwave troughs pass by 
to our north. These two shortwaves show up nicely on water vapor
imagery early this morning as a pair of closed circulations 
embedded with a broader trough extending from southern 
Saskatchewan into the Pacific Northwest. Associated sfc low will
track east into Manitoba today with a cold front trailing south
into the lower Missouri Valley by later this afternoon. 

Out ahead of this system, southern winds will become 
established across our CWA today leading to another unseasonably
warm day. Despite cirrus cloudiness obscuring the sun a bit, 
still anticipate high temps to climb into the mid to upper 80s 
today. With deeper low level moisture pooled ahead of the 
boundary to our west, we could see dewpoints mix out some this 
afternoon, especially eastern CWA, which should keep heat 
indices near or a hair below ambient temperatures. 

Convection is expected to develop over IA this afternoon ahead 
of the cold front in an area of maximized instability and 
moderate shear. This convection is expected to move eastward 
into northern Illinois tonight, but as it does so, it will be 
moving into a more stable environment with less moisture. In 
addition, the lead shortwave will be lifting farther northeast, 
becoming even more removed from what will likely be a decaying 
convective complex moving into northern IL overnight. The low 
level jet is expected to be focused to our north and also not be
of much assistance in maintaining the intensity of this MCS as 
it moves into our area. With MUCAPE expected to be 500 J/kg or 
less, there may not be much thunder left with this activity as 
it moves into our area. 

The remnants of that activity could linger into Wednesday 
morning over our area, mainly bringing a threat of showers 
without much threat for thunder. Wednesday's set-up looks 
potentially pretty messy, with the potential for outflow from 
this prior convection resulting in an effective frontal boundary
setting up over central IL into north central Indiana Wednesday
afternoon, well ahead of the synoptic cold front which is 
progged to move into northern IL during the afternoon. Mid and 
upper level height falls in advance of trailing shortwave trough
is likely to support renewed convective development Wednesday 
afternoon into Wednesday evening, but it isn't clear if the more
widespread and stronger convection will be over central IL with
the lead outflow boundary or if the air mass in the wake of 
that boundary will recover sufficiently allowing the true 
synoptic cold front to be the primary focus for late day into 
evening storms. 

Mid-level lapse rates should remain pretty weak Wednesday, 
limiting instability despite 70F+ dewpoints likely to be pooling
near and ahead of the boundary/boundaries. That degree of low 
level moisture is still likely to support an axis of 1000-1500 
J/kg of MLCAPE (given sufficient heating/breaks in the 
cloudiness). The moderate instability paired with respectable 
deep layer shear around 40kt, could lead to a localized threat 
for severe storms Wednesday afternoon, particularly over our 
southern CWA as it looks now. The showers and thunderstorms 
should gradually settle south of our CWA Wednesday night as the 
synoptic front pushes south of the area. 

In the wake of the front, look for a brief cool down and return
to temperatures closer to average Thursday. Warm air advection 
is already progged to start ramping up Friday in advance of the 
next shortwave, allowing temps to warm a bit Friday and more so 
into Saturday. The next cold front should move across the 
region later Saturday or Saturday night bringing with it the 
next chance of showers/storms followed by another return to near
average temps late in the weekend into early next week.

- Izzi
